Subject: Re: MAP: final sizing ask — GPU mix, regional targets, and eval runbook

Adding perf / kernel notes from Marcus (serving runtime):

- Rationale for H100S primary: the model family EdgeHealth plans to use has long contexts and benefits from H100S attention kernels. The 8x H100S baseline gives predictable latency at the target sequence lengths.
- A100-80GB in west is cost-effective for burst and regional failover; we recommend q4 INT8 profiles for most endpoints.
- Contention assumptions: we modeled 40% KV cache hits and 20% request coalescing — real traffic may push effective throughput +/-15%.

Throughput targets (model-level assumptions):
- baseline per-H100S: ~1.5k tokens/sec (sustained) => 8x = 12k aggregate
- burst per-H100S (with larger batch windows): ~2.5k tokens/sec => 8x = 20k burst
- A100 baseline per-GPU: ~1.0k tokens/sec => 4x = 4k baseline

I've attached microbench notes and a CSV of per-model profiles. If EdgeHealth wants tighter SLOs we can propose an alternative with 12x H100S baseline (would raise costs but reduce P95 latency).

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Quick note on eval runbook and acceptance gates from the applied ML side:

- Eval runbook highlights (to include in eval_runbook_EH.md):
  1) Sanity checks: model load, end-to-end 1-token warmup, sample inference for 10 prompts.
  2) Perf tests: 5-minute sustained traffic at baseline QPS (target tokens/sec) with P95 latency < 220ms for standard prompts.
  3) Regression checks: run the provided prompt set (20 prompts) and compare top-1 token distribution drift — thresholds at >5% drift trigger investigation.
  4) Resource checks: GPU memory pressure, host CPU utilization, KV cache hit rate (>35% expected).

- Example commands and expected outputs will be in the runbook. I'll add a short section on quantization caveats (INT8 may reduce mem but can affect tail probability on edge-case prompts).

I'll review the v2 sheet now and expect to sign off on the numbers.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Applied ML — Redwood Inference
